source.name: Hardcore punk
source.lineage: Early-1980s American underground extension of punk into faster tempos, shorter song lengths, screamed vocals, and a developed touring-and-DIY-record-label network — codified through the Washington DC scene (Bad Brains Bad Brains 1982, Minor Threat — Out of Step 1983), the Boston scene (SS Decontrol, DYS), the Los Angeles scene (Black Flag — Damaged 1981, Circle Jerks, Suicidal Tendencies), and the New York hardcore scene (Agnostic Front, Cro-Mags, Sick of It All)

extras.description: Hardcore punk (codified 1979-1985 American suburban-and-urban punk-evolution scenes — Black Flag's Los Angeles, Minor Threat's Washington DC, Bad Brains's DC-and-NYC, Dead Kennedys's San Francisco), the faster-and-angrier-than-punk underground subgenre. Defined by tempos pushed to 180-220 BPM (faster than first-wave punk's 140-180 BPM), shouted-vocal delivery without melodic singing, song-lengths often under 2 minutes with extreme economy of structure, breakdowns mid-song where the rhythm halves and the riff opens (the breakdown that fed forward into metalcore), DIY-zine-and-fanzine distribution and small-club tour circuit, and lyric content addressing political-radical-anarchist themes, suburban-malaise, and confrontational-social-commentary. Distinguished from first-wave punk by speed and tighter performance economy; distinguished from later metalcore by absence of metal-derived guitar-tone; distinguished from grindcore by retention of punk-rock structural conventions over extreme-short-form fusion.

source.name: Stoner metal
source.lineage: Southern California desert-rock-derived heavy-blues-revival genre that emerged in early-1990s Palm Desert and Los Angeles — codified through Kyuss (the founding band from Palm Desert, Welcome to Sky Valley 1994), Queens of the Stone Age (Josh Hommes post-Kyuss continuation, Songs for the Deaf 2002), Sleep (the Bay Area parallel canon, Sleeps Holy Mountain 1992 and the legendary 60-minute single-track Dopesmoker 2003), Fu Manchu, Monster Magnet; built on Sabbath chord vocabulary plus blues-rock pentatonic vocabulary plus down-tuned heavy-fuzz amplifier worship

extras.description: Stoner metal / stoner rock (codified 1990s onward through Kyuss, Sleep, and Fu Manchu establishing the California-desert sound, with continuous tradition through to present and parallel doom-stoner-and-stoner-rock subgenres), the early-1970s English heavy-blues-rock-derived psychedelic riff music subgenre. Defined by downtuned guitars (drop-C, drop-B, or further detunings) producing thick low-end heaviness, bluesy modal-pentatonic riff vocabulary drawn from Sabbath-and-early-70s heavy-blues-rock heritage, fuzz-and-wah pedal-effected guitar tone with extended sustain, vocal performance often clean-melodic with light-distortion or psychedelic-effected processing, song-form built on extended riff-progression with extended jam-improvisation sections (the Kyuss desert-jam-aesthetic), tempos around 90-120 BPM, and lyric and visual themes addressing cannabis-culture, desert-and-southwest landscape, and psychedelic-mystical experience. Distinguished from straight doom by faster tempo and retention of clean-melodic vocal; distinguished from drone-doom by song-form structure; distinguished from psychedelic-rock by post-1990 timestamp and metal-derived guitar-tone weight.

source.name: Hard rock
source.lineage: Late-1960s through 1980s UK and US hard rock canon codified through Led Zeppelin (Led Zeppelin II 1969 anchoring the heavy-blues-derived foundation), Deep Purple (Machine Head 1972), Black Sabbath (the heavier sludge-pioneering wing), Aerosmith (the US blues-rock crossover), Van Halen (Eddie Van Halens technical-guitar virtuoso revolution from 1978 onward), AC/DC (the Australian-Scottish stripped-down hard rock canon, Back in Black 1980)

extras.description: Hard rock (codified late-1968 through 1973 in the UK and US, descending from blues-rock and psychedelic-rock and crystallizing through Cream-Hendrix-Led-Zeppelin-Deep-Purple-Black-Sabbath-Mountain-Grand-Funk lineage), the amplified blues-rock subgenre. Defined by fifth-interval riff vocabulary (the I-V power-chord shape replacing earlier blues-rock's full triadic chord-voicings), shouted-and-wailed high-projection vocal delivery often with blues-rock-derived melismatic ornamentation, concussive bass-drum-and-snare backbeat with prominent fills and tom-foreground percussion, distorted Marshall-stack guitar tone (Big Muff and pre-amp gain-stage saturation), song-forms built on extended verse-chorus with riff-based bridge sections, and tempos around 100-130 BPM. Distinguished from psychedelic-rock by absence of mind-expansion lyrical apparatus and tighter song-form; distinguished from heavy metal (which descends from it) by retention of blues-rock vocabulary and absence of tritone occult-and-dissonant material; distinguished from punk by virtuosic-not-amateur instrumental aesthetic.

source.name: Grunge
source.lineage: Seattle Pacific Northwest alternative-rock genre that emerged in the late 1980s and went global in 1991 — codified through Nirvana (Nevermind 1991, the commercial breakthrough produced by Butch Vig), Pearl Jam (Ten 1991), Soundgarden (Badmotorfinger 1991, then Superunknown 1994), Alice in Chains (Facelift 1990, Dirt 1992), Mudhoney (the Sub Pop founding band), Screaming Trees, Tad — built on a fusion of hardcore punk aggression and Sabbath-style heavy-blues-derived guitar tone

extras.description: Grunge (codified 1985-1995 Seattle and broader Pacific Northwest, with first-wave Sub Pop label era and second-wave major-label commercial breakthrough through Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, and Alice in Chains), the late-1980s/early-1990s hybrid of punk, hardcore, and metal. Defined by Sabbath-derived heavy-blues-rock riff vocabulary translated through hardcore-punk-and-college-rock sensibility, alternation between quiet verse and loud chorus dynamic structure (the soft-loud signature established by the Pixies and adapted), distorted-fuzz-pedal electric-guitar tone (Big Muff fuzz, MXR Distortion+), apathetic-or-distressed vocal delivery, lyric content of generational disaffection, depression, and Pacific-Northwest-suburban-malaise, and college-rock-and-indie-label production aesthetic transitioning into major-label commercial sound 1991 onward. Distinguished from straight metal by punk-and-college-rock lineage; distinguished from hardcore punk by retention of heavy-blues-rock guitar; distinguished from Britpop by US-not-UK origin and darker-and-grungier aesthetic.

source.name: Death metal
source.lineage: Mid-1980s onward extreme metal subgenre characterized by down-tuned humbucker guitar, palm-muted chug riffs, blast-beat drumming, growl-vocal delivery, and morbid thematic content — codified through Florida-tampa-bay (Death — Scream Bloody Gore 1987, Morbid Angel — Altars of Madness 1989, Obituary, Deicide), and Stockholm (Entombed — Left Hand Path 1990, Dismember, Grave) with the genre splitting into technical, brutal, and melodic substreams by the mid-1990s

extras.description: Death metal (1985 onward, codified 1989-1993 through Florida (Tampa-Death-Obituary) and Stockholm (Entombed-Dismember-Grave) regional scenes), the downtuned blast-beat-driven extreme metal subgenre. Defined by guitars tuned down (D, C, B, A standard or further), tremolo-picked dissonant riffs in mid-low register exploiting half-step and tritone intervals, blast-beat percussion alternating bass-drum-and-snare at 200+ BPM, growled or guttural-grunted vocal delivery far below conversational pitch (the death-growl that names the genre), song-form built on riff-juxtaposition rather than verse-chorus and frequent metric-modulation, and lyrical content treating mortality, gore, occult, and existential-philosophical material. Distinguished from black metal by mid-low-not-treble emphasis and growled-not-shrieked vocal; distinguished from doom by blast-beat tempo; distinguished from grindcore by song-length and progressive-metal structural ambition; distinguished from thrash by absence of major-key punk-derived vocabulary.

source.name: Folk black metal
source.lineage: Folk-inflected black-metal practice represented by Windir’s Sogn-centered repertoire. Season of Mist describes their black/heavy-metal music with old Norwegian folk elements and documents the four 1997-2003 albums and the shift to a full band on 1184. The compact authored seed carries folk-facing melodic continuity through guitar and voice rather than inferring a compulsory folk-instrument ensemble.

extras.description: Folk black metal applies folk-derived melodic and narrative orientation inside a black-metal ensemble. Windir is the selected anchor: the label documents old Norwegian folk elements, regional Sogn identity and the full-band 1184 milestone. The default authors ringing tremolo melody, steady bass, sticks and a rough sung voice. It does not claim a collected traditional tune, ethnic vocal technique or compulsory accordion, pipes or bowed lyres. Unlike pagan_metal’s expansive folk-instrument and chorus roster, this is a compact black-metal band model; unlike atmospheric_black_metal, melodic and regional repertoire identity leads rather than a long diffuse soundfield. The Sogn marker describes this exemplar network, not the location of every folk-black-metal scene.
